provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The original rule: each row has a coloured cell at its left end and its right end. If the two cells are the same non-background colour, the whole row is filled with that colour. A horizontal flip (d4>=4) leaves rows as rows and simply swaps which end is which. The comparison is symmetric, so the flip changes nothing. An odd number of clockwise rotations turns the rows into columns, so the endpoints move to the top and bottom rows. In that case the emitted program compares g[0,x] with g[h-1,x] and fills column x. For even rotations it compares g[y,0] with g[y,w-1] and fills row y. The background is fixed at palette[0], which is the image of original colour 0. A line is drawn only when its endpoints match and are not background. All indices come from the actual grid height and width, so rectangular shapes work.
draft_notes.limitations: I have not run any tests. The program assumes the generator's domain: endpoint cells lie only on the two grid edges perpendicular to the line direction, and the background is palette[0]. I chose the axis from d4 rather than inferring it from the demonstrations. The fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule, and I found no contradictions.
